Tarryn Aiken (centre) is mobbed by teammates after scoring in the NRLW grand final. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

The 2026 Sydney Roosters NRLW side has cemented its legacy with a crushing grand final win over the Brisbane Broncos.

Twelve months on from a heartbreaking loss to the women from Brisbane, the Roosters not only won the premiership, but did something no other top-flight rugby league team has achieved in Australia for more than a century.

Here are the quick hits from Sydney's NRLW grand final win over Brisbane.

It doesn't matter how much experience you have, every player feels some sort of pressure on grand final day.

And the pressure of a grand final was on display in the opening minutes, with a pair of State of Origin representatives making uncharacteristic errors.

Ali Brigginshaw's decorated rugby league career ended with a heavy defeat but there can be no doubt about the impact the Broncos playmaker has had on the game.

Sydney Roosters winger Jayme Fressard had a proper shocker to begin the grand final, failing to gather the opening kick-off and nudging it into touch.

As the ball came to the NSW State of Origin rep, she tried to trap it with her foot but kicked the footy over the sideline.

The Roosters were able to defend their goal-line and then it was a Broncos Origin rep to have a shocker.

It was Fressard's opposing winger, Julia Robinson, who dropped the ball stone cold in her own half, which gifted the Roosters a golden chance to open the scoring.

Unlike the Broncos, the Roosters were able to score when winger Brydie Parker fielded a great cross-field kick from five-eighth Jocelyn Kelleher and touched down in the corner.

The Roosters were dominating the grand final in the first half, as multiple errors from Brisbane kept them under immense pressure.

But Brisbane's goal-line defence was one aspect of their game that was withstanding the impressive Roosters.

That was until Sydney halfback Tarryn Aiken, who missed last year's decider due to an ACL injury, produced three moments of brilliance in a 7-minute stretch that led to a trio of tries for the Roosters.

First Aiken grubbered for herself and when the ball bounced off the arm of Brisbane winger Kerri Johnson, the Sydney halfback caught the ricochet and scored the game's second try.

Four minutes later, Aiken was setting up the third try of the match. The halfback lined up at lock in an attacking scrum 10 metres from Brisbane's goal-line. Aiken passed from the base of the scrum to the left, wrapped around and retook the footy, then gave a perfect short pass to captain Isabelle Kelly who charged over.

The Roosters then charged down the field again and when a sixth tackle play looked to be coming unstuck, it was Aiken again who produced a great kick which Brisbane's Deleni Paitai fumbled, and the Tricolours regathered and Fressard scored in the corner.

The trailblazing career of Ali Brigginshaw, someone who has been instrumental in the growth of women's rugby league, came to an end with an NRLW grand final.

But the legendary Broncos, Maroos and Jillaroo might have considered herself lucky not to have been sin-binned in her farewell game.

With the Roosters on top, Brigginshaw was desperate not to let Aiken put in an attacking cross-field kick.
